title: Kara and Nate
description: Husband-and-wife travel filmmakers Kara and Nate Rice, who left Nashville in 2016 for a one-year trip that turned into more than a hundred countries: overland expeditions, long-distance train journeys, wildlife encounters and road trips, from the Mongol Rally across Central Asia to Patagonia, Oman, Iceland and the Australian Outback.
creator: Kara and Nate (Kara and Nate Rice)

episodes.title: WHY WE DON’T VISIT NATIONAL PARKS (road trip to Oregon)
episodes.description:
We are really sad, but we also respect the rules even though it’s tough. Thank y’all for listening. Regardless, we are excited to explore more of our beautiful country as we continue west!

Our time in Utah and Idaho were very brief, and now you know why. Both are lovely states we can't wait to revisit hopefully soon!

After 2 years of saving $ and over 2 million miles and points, we sold our cars and apartment and left home January 10, 2016. We started this #travelvlog to share our experiences with friends and family, then decided we really liked vlogging and traveling! After achieving our new goal of 100 countries before 2020 and all 7 continents, we have no plans to slow down anytime soon, and we are incredibly thankful to do something we love every day. :)

episodes.title: TRADING OUR VAN FOR A CONVERTED SCHOOL BUS (full tour)
episodes.description:
Should we have bought a school bus instead of a van? In this episode, we see what it's like to live in a gorgeous converted "skoolie." Back in March when our lives were flipped upside down, we had no idea what we were going to do this year. We ALMOST bought a converted school bus, so today we're comparing #vanlife to #buslife to see if we made the right decision ;)

The owners of this bus have a YouTube channel where they documented the entire conversion process and their adventures in it, check them out :) https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCSkaz0jjb7s07QO94GPH0Tw

After 2 years of saving $ and over 2 million miles and points, we sold our cars and apartment and left home January 10, 2016. We started this #travelvlog to share our experiences with friends and family, then decided we really liked vlogging and traveling, and we didn’t want to stop after just one year! After achieving our new goal of 100 countries and then all 7 continents (check out our documentary here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FuFv4iF8wgg&t=1s), we had no plans to slow down, until 2020 decided to force us to ;) which is when we bought a converted Sprinter van to start exploring our own country for the first time. #Vanlife was a major adjustment and so different than flying every week like we were used to, but we are incredibly thankful to be able to continue doing something we love every day. 😊🎥🌎

👩🏻‍🍳 KARA'S FAMOUS ONE POT PEANUT BUTTER RAMEN RECIPE!

I'm usually a biiiig measuring cup kind of girl, but for some reason with this recipe, I don't measure anything and taste it along the way. The ingredients change every time. Have fun with it!!! 😋

This is for 2 servings (keep in mind i have no idea what i'm doing):

Ingredients:
Olive oil (or whatever you like)
4ish Garlic cloves
1ish inch fresh Ginger 
2 of your favorite instant ramens
Salt
Pepper
Coconut aminos
Cayenne pepper
Peanut butter
Fresh Cilantro 
Green onions 
Toasted sesame seeds
Sriracha

1. Sauté the garlic and ginger with some olive oil
2. Add water (or veg broth!) and make the “sauce”
3. Add the seasoning package that comes with the ramen if you want, or make your own:
4. Add coconut aminos (Idk, maybe 1/3 cup?), salt, pepper, cayenne (if using soy sauce, you don't need as much or any salt!). You could also add the chopped green onions here to cook In the sauce
5. Stir in 1ish scoop of peanut butter
6. Add in noods and let it all cook together
7. Put in bowls and add fresh cilantro, green onion, sesame seeds, and sriracha!

episodes.title: OUR FIRST IMPRESSIONS OF MEXICO VAN LIFE
episodes.description:
Episode 817 | Baja, Mexico | Filmed March 2022

Watch our whole Baja series here: https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLirGII1_qwvuW34iM3PE1u4GO-ynx_v1m

This video is days 4-6 of our van life road trip to the tip of the Baja peninsula! We left our beautiful cliffside campsite near Ensenada and filled up the van with diesel for the first time, ate street tacos, stocked up on popsicles, and got stopped at our first military check point. Then we headed south to Bahia de Los Angeles where we wild camped for the first time. AKA we slept on a beautiful secluded beach for FREE?! We accidentally went 3 days off the grid without internet, and by day 4 we finally made our way to a cafe to check in with our families who were worried about us ;) That's where we met our new friends, @Mrandmrsadventure ❤️ Check out their channel for the ultimate 3 month Baja trip! They gave us tons of tips for the rest of our time here ☀️

Originally from Nashville, Tennessee, we got married 2013 and were super “normal.” I was a teacher and Nate started a small printing business from the spare bedroom of our apartment. Who are Kara and Nate?! 
Watch our documentary here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FuFv4iF8wgg&t=1s

Originally from Nashville, Tennessee, we got married 2013 and were super “normal.” I was a teacher and Nate started a small printing business from the spare bedroom of our apartment. We discovered the world of “travel hacking” & became obsessed. So after 2 years of obsessively saving $35k and over 2 million miles and points, we sold our cars and apartment and left home January 10, 2016 for a “one year” trip around the world. Our goal was to see as many places as possible before we ran out of money and went home to “normal life.” We started this travel vlog to share our experiences with friends and family, but quickly fell in love with this lifestyle and did everything we could to keep going. 4 years later, we achieved our new goal of visiting 100 countries and all 7 continents. We had no plans to slow down, until 2020 forced us to ;) Which is when we bought a converted van to start exploring our own country for the first time. Van life was a major adjustment and so different than flying every week like we were used to, but we are incredibly thankful to be able to continue doing something we love every day. 😊🎥🌎

episodes.title: AMERICAN FOOTBALL VS. EUROPEAN FOOTBALL (We Went to the Biggest Rivalry Games)
episodes.description:
We flew to Spain to answer this question: American Football vs. European "Soccer" - which is better?! We found out by going to the biggest rivalry game on both continents: Real Madrid vs. Barcelona ⚽️ & Tennessee Vols vs. Florida Gators 🏈 The two experiences were WAY different than we expected! Which sport do you prefer?! Special thanks to Rocket Learn for sponsoring this episode! Check out the latest episode of Home Lore here: https://youtu.be/PpZmD_5Le0A 

We grew up watching American Football and have always wanted to go to a "soccer" game (calling it soccer to prevent confusion ;)). 

The Tennessee Vols and Florida Gators have been rival teams for awhile now, and Tennessee is actually good this year, so we thought that'd be a great game to go watch in real life.

Then we learned that Real Madrid and Barcelona were going to be playing each other (AKA El Clasico!) WHILE we were in Spain! 

We had the best time sharing game day at our alma mater, AND getting to experience our very first "soccer" game with our new friend Yoanna!

At the end of the day, even though these 2 sports are very different from each other, our favorite part was seeing people (and complete strangers) from all over the world at both events bonding, putting their differences aside, and having a great time together :) 

Did any of our comparisons surprise you? Comment below annd let us know which experience youd prefer :)
￼

episodes.title: We Visited the Most Remote Town in Australia
episodes.description:
We drove a truck camper drove over 1,000 km through the Outback to Australia’s most remote town! (part 1) Go to our sponsor https://betterhelp.com/kandn for 10% off your first month of therapy with BetterHelp and get matched with a therapist who will listen and help :) 

Watch PART 2 here!! - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OZ9cpQ1PWBU 

We rented our car through Adventure Rentals! Check them out: https://adventurerentals.com.au/?utm_medium=youtube_source=karaandnateyoutube_campaign=karaandnate

*PLEASE read the details below if you are planning your own roadtrip here* :) 
Aboriginal held land in Australia is private property and to travel through, you need permission often in the form of a permit. For Kiwirrkurra Country, a permit allows you to travel along the main road, into community and camp at approved campsites. Access into any other areas aside from this is still prohibited. More information on traveling through Kiwirrkurra country can be found at https://www.tjamutjamu.com/travelling-to-kiwirrkurra-country and https://kiwirrkurra.au/. The Kiwirrkurra Traditional Owners thank you for respecting their culture and country.

ALSO! If you are looking to buy Aboriginal art, make sure you buy from the most ethical sources which are community artist-owned art galleries and collectives. For Kiwirrkurra art you can purchase through Papunya Tula Artists (https://papunyatula.com.au/). For other Central Australian Aboriginal art, visit Desart for more information at https://desart.com.au/ Thank you :)

—

*PLEASE read the details below if you are planning your own road trip here* :) 

Aboriginal held land in Australia is private property and to travel through, you need permission often in the form of a permit. For Kiwirrkurra Country, a permit allows you to travel along the main road, into community and camp at approved campsites. Access into any other areas aside from this is still prohibited. More information on traveling through Kiwirrkurra country can be found at https://www.tjamutjamu.com/travelling-to-kiwirrkurra-country and https://kiwirrkurra.au/. The Kiwirrkurra Traditional Owners thank you for respecting their culture and country.

ALSO! If you are looking to buy Aboriginal art, make sure you buy from the most ethical sources which are community artist-owned art galleries and collectives. For Kiwirrkurra art you can purchase through Papunya Tula Artists (https://papunyatula.com.au/). For other Central Australian Aboriginal art, visit Desart for more information at https://desart.com.au/ Thank you :)
